transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um... well, I guess what brings me in is... I've just been having this sort of constant restless feeling? It's probably just me overthinking it, or maybe just stress, but I feel like I'm wound a little too tight, and I just can't seem to fully settle. 

It happens even when I'm doing things where I'm supposed to be completely calm—like, um, sitting through a long planning meeting for work, or even during my downtime, like when I'm painting or trying to do yoga. I just can't quite relax into it like I'm supposed to. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it very well, but I just thought I should probably ask someone about it to make sure I'm doing okay.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been going on for weeks, or more like several months or longer?

Um, well... I suppose it's been going on for a bit longer than a few months. I'd say it's been noticeably harder to manage for about... maybe two years and two months? Give or take? 

It kind of lines up with when we started having some, um... well, some family stress. Just some conflicts with my in-laws that started taking over more of our evenings. I'm sure everyone gets a little restless when they're dealing with family stuff, right? I really hope I'm not just making a big deal out of normal everyday stress. Does that sound like a normal reaction to you?

Would you say your worry and restlessness is mainly focused on the situation with your in-laws, or do you also find yourself excessively worrying about other things—like work, health, or finances—that aren't related to that conflict?

Um, no, I don't think so. I really try not to be a worrier, to be honest. I mean, everyone thinks about work or bills sometimes, right? Especially in my job—I'm a retail buyer, so things can get pretty fast-paced—but I definitely wouldn't say I worry about it excessively. I actually think I handle all that day-to-day stuff pretty well. 

It's really more of a... a physical feeling, I guess? Like my motor is just always running, rather than my mind actually spinning about bad things happening. Even with the in-law situation, I'm not sitting around agonizing over it, I just... I just feel extra fidgety and have a harder time sitting still when things get tense. 

I hope I'm explaining the difference right. I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about normal life stuff when I actually have it pretty good. Does that make sense to you? That it's more of a physical restlessness rather than actually being anxious about things?
Do you notice this restless, wound-up feeling even during periods when things with your in-laws are calm or you're not thinking about that situation at all?

Oh, um... gosh, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really paid close enough attention to notice if it happens when things are completely calm with them. 

I guess I usually just try to push through and keep busy, so I haven't tracked it very well. I'm sorry, I hope that's not a frustrating answer? I know I should probably be more observant about my own body, but I just haven't really noticed one way or the other. Is it okay that I don't have a better answer for that?

Besides this restless, keyed-up feeling, have you also noticed things like trouble sleeping, feeling easily fatigued, difficulty concentrating, irritability, or muscle tension on most days over these past couple of years?

Um, well... I don't really think so. I mean, I sleep okay, usually. And I don't feel like I'm more tired than anyone else my age. I'm 51, so I think getting a little tired after a long day is just part of getting older, right? 

And as for concentrating or being irritable... I really try my best to stay positive and focused at work. I wouldn't say I have a hard time with those things on most days. I really don't want to sound like I'm falling apart or anything! I think I manage pretty well overall. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just don't think I have those other problems you mentioned.

Over the past couple of years, would you say this restless, wound-up feeling has been present on most days—even days when nothing in particular is stressing you out—or does it really only show up when something specific is going on?

Um, well... I guess I'd have to say it's mostly just when something specific is going on. I really don't think I feel that way on most days. I try to be pretty easygoing, you know? 

I mean, everyone has days where they feel a little antsy or need to move around, but I definitely wouldn't say it's an everyday thing for me, especially if there's no real reason for it. I really try to keep a good attitude and not let things get to me too much. 

I hope I'm answering that right? I just don't want you to think I'm constantly on edge or anything like that, because I really do think I handle things pretty well most of the time. Is that helpful?

When you notice this restless, keyed-up feeling, is it pretty much always connected to something happening with the in-law situation, or have you noticed it flaring up around other stressful events too, unrelated to your in-laws?

Um, gosh, that's a good question. I... I think it's mostly just the in-law stuff, really. I mean, maybe occasionally if work gets super busy, but... I don't think it really flares up with other things. 

I try to take things in stride, you know? I don't want to make a big deal out of every little stressor that comes along. I really think I'm pretty good at managing regular day-to-day things without getting all worked up. I'm sorry, I hope that makes sense? I just don't want to give the impression that I'm easily rattled by everything, because I really don't think I am. Is it okay that it's mostly just tied to that one situation?

Have there been any stretches of time—maybe a week or more—when things with your in-laws were resolved or not an issue at all, and if so, did that restless, wound-up feeling go away during those periods?

Um, well... yes, there definitely have been times when things were quiet on that front. Like, if they go on a trip or we just don't have any family events for a couple of weeks. And, um, yeah, I'd say I feel totally fine during those times. 

I really do think I bounce back pretty quickly once the stress is gone. I just go back to my normal self, you know? I don't hold onto it or stay all wound up. I try to just let it go and enjoy the peace and quiet. 

I hope that's a good sign? I really like to think of myself as a resilient person, and I don't want you to think this is something that just takes over my whole life. I manage okay when things are normal, I really do. Does that sound right to you?

Symptoms are clearly stressor-contingent: they remit fully during stretches when the stressor is absent, and are not present pervasively on most days independent of the stressor, arguing against Generalized Anxiety Disorder. The reaction is out of proportion in duration (linked directly and exclusively to a specific ongoing stressor) with clear symptomatic and functional distress (restlessness impairing ability to relax during meetings, hobbies), fulfilling criteria for Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety, chronic subtype given the persistence of the stressor beyond 6 months.
